item.title: 49ers-Seahawks roundtable: How much will who's under center matter?
item.description: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks passes the ball while being pressured by Romello Height #94 of the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter at Lumen Field on Oct. 11, 2026 in Seattle. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images) When the San Francisco 49ers traveled to Seattle to play the Seahawks seven weeks ago, it represented a big moment for both teams. The 49ers won, remaining undefeated, and have gone 4-1 since. After narrowly losing, the Seahawks have stumbled to 3-2. With Kyle Shanahan 's club riding high and leading the NFC but facing a game with Brock Purdy on the sidelines, we asked columnist Ann Killion and reporters Eric Branch and Harrison Rich for their answers to these key questions going into Sunday's rematch. First, a general NFL question: the drama in Pittsburgh. Have we seen the last of Aaron Rodgers in uniform? Harrison Rich: It's often hard to side with Aaron Rodgers, but he seems to have the stronger argument here over Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. ESPN confirmed Rodgers' allegations against McCarthy , including sleeping in quarterback meetings and breaking down a halftime huddle by saying "1-2-3 Packers." Rodgers was waived Wednesday, but I'd imagine he plays football again in 2026 - assuming he wants to. He was still playing at a fairly high level and led Pittsburgh to a 6-4 record before his ousting. Eric Branch: The constant in Aaron Rodgers' family and work drama: Aaron Rodgers. Given the late-career strife he's often been responsible for causing, it's notable that Rodgers' 22-season career began with him spending three good-soldier seasons sitting behind Brett Favre. Rodgers took a flamethrower to his long relationship with Mike McCarthy. It sounds as if much of what he alleged is true, but he broke an NFL code and left his playoff-contending teammates to deal with the fallout. Has he played his last snap? Not if an injury to a starting QB creates an urgent need. As former Cardinals GM Steve Keim once said of NFL teams rationalizing character concerns: "If Hannibal Lecter ran a 4.3, we'd probably diagnose it as an eating disorder." Ann Killion: I wouldn't be shocked if some playoff-bound team suffers an injury at quarterback and brings Rodgers in. I mean, who would be better? But, as the Black Friday broadcast team pointed out, Rodgers had already said this is his last year and has also emphasized that when he was done playing he will pull a "Keyser Soze" and disappear from public view. (Interesting to hear fellow former Cal Bear Tony Gonzalez put Rodgers on blast.) Yet there he was, airing his dirty laundry on the Pat McAfee show, blowtorching the coach he won a Super Bowl with, and texting Al Michaels during the Friday broadcast to further litigate his case. The guy desperately needs the spotlight. Pittsburgh crushed Denver, sending the message that they don't need Rodgers (though the players all still seem to like him). Rodgers' most amazing feat? Turning hapless McCarthy into a sympathetic character. Fred Warner

item.title: WNBA Star Caitlin Clark Reacts to Dallas Cowboys’ Loss to Philadelphia Eagles
item.description: Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark was among those left puzzled by the Dallas Cowboys’ late-game decisions during their Thanksgiving collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles. The WNBA guard reacted to the 39-38 defeat on social media, questioning what Dallas was attempting to accomplish during the closing moments. Clark followed the Cowboys-Eagles matchup before turning her attention to the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills’ Thanksgiving night game. Her reaction came after Philadelphia erased a 21-point deficit to complete one of the most remarkable comebacks in the NFL’s Thanksgiving history. Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark (22) cheers on Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell (0) after a basket Friday, Sept. 26, 2025, during Game 3 of the WNBA semifinals against the Las Vegas Aces at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. Dallas appeared to have secured control of the contest after taking a 31-10 lead in the third quarter. The Cowboys continued to hold the advantage late in the fourth, leading 38-36 with less than a minute remaining. However, head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s decision on fourth-and-1 created an opportunity for Philadelphia to take control. Rather than attempting to punt or protect the lead through another approach, Dallas kept its offense on the field with 55 seconds remaining. Quarterback Dak Prescott was subsequently sacked for a nine-yard loss, giving the Eagles possession in favorable field position. Philadelphia capitalized on the opportunity, with kicker Jake Elliott converting a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left. WNBA Star Caitlin Clark Reacts to Dallas Cowboys’ Loss to Philadelphia Eagles Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark (22) arrives Tuesday, Sept. 16, 2025, before Game 2 of a WNBA playoff matchup between the Indiana Fever and the Atlanta Dream at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. Clark shared her thoughts about Dallas’ loss to the Eagles on Thanksgiving. This can be seen in a post she shared on X. “What exactly were the cowboys doing there,” Clark wrote. Clark posted a brief question about the Cowboys’ decision , reflecting the confusion shared by many viewers following the sequence. Although she did not identify a particular player or coach in her message, the timing suggested her reaction was connected to Dallas’ costly fourth-down attempt. The defeat was particularly damaging because the Cowboys had controlled much of the matchup before allowing Philadelphia to rally. Clark’s reaction added another prominent name to the growing discussion surrounding Dallas’ Thanksgiving collapse, which left the franchise searching for answers after a painful divisional loss. item.title: Central Bucks West shuts out Spring-Ford, wins district championship
item.description: DOYLESTOWN — Central Bucks West played for its sixth PIAA District One football championship on Friday night. The Bucks won District One onfield titles under Mike Pettine in 1993 and 1997-99, as well as Mike Carey in 2000. Spring-Ford, like CB West, went into the game at War Memorial Field with identical 12-1 records. The Bucks finished the job, downing the Rams 34-0 behind a dominant rushing attack and suffocating defense. Senior Lou Cipollo ran for a pair of touchdowns while seniors Nick Miletto and Braylen Cope both scored a rushing touchdown. CB West will face the St. Joseph Prep/Nazareth winner in next weekend’s Class 6A semifinals. Prep led Nazareth 49-20 at the start of the fourth quarter. West had reached the district title game in 2022, when it lost at Garnet Valley, while Spring-Ford fell to Coatesville for the 2012 district championship. This is the Bucks' first district title in 26 seasons. Rob Rowan’s CB West squad defeated Perkiomen Valley 56-42, Central Bucks East 44-21 and Council Rock South 30-13 to reach the final, while Spring-Ford topped Quakertown 42-28, Plymouth Whitemarsh 28-21 and top-seeded Downingtown East 17-14 at districts. *Check back later tonight for much more on the game. What’s next for Spring-Ford Football? The season ended for the Rams. What’s next for Central Bucks West Football? The Bucks will face St. Joseph Prep or Nazareth in the state semifinals next weekend. item.title: Mangiapane Scores Twice, Blackhawks Beat Rangers For Fourth Straight Win
item.description: The Chicago Blackhawks (10-14-2) tied a franchise record for the fewest shots recorded in a regular-season game with 10, but it was enough to defeat the New York Rangers (13-11-1) 2-1 at the United Center on Friday. Andrew Mangiapane scored both of Chicago’s goals, his first two tallies of the season, Oliver Moore had two assists, and Spencer Knight stopped 30 of 31 shots as the Blackhawks extended their winning streak to four games. The Blackhawks are now 6-1-1 in eight games since an abysmal 0-3 Southeastern road trip earlier this month. Mika Zibanejad scored for the Rangers, while Dylan Garand started in net and allowed two goals on 10 shots faced. Adam Fox extended his point streak to five games with an assist on Zibanejad’s power-play goal. All three goals in Friday’s game were power-play tallies, with the Blackhawks converting on both opportunities and extending their goal streak to eight games. Since opening the season with a 5-for-51 stretch, the power play has now scored on 13 of its last 22 opportunities. Even without Patrick Kane and Tyler Bertuzzi , the man advantage continued its red-hot stretch, and it was the second unit stepping up to score both goals against the Rangers. Entering Friday, New York had the NHL’s top-ranked penalty kill and had allowed a league-low three power-play goals in their first 12 road games. But even without their best offensive players, including captain Connor Bedard and Bowen Byram , the power play impressively still found a way to generate all the offense needed against a stout Rangers’ PK for a fourth straight win. Defensively, Knight was outstanding for the second straight game, as the 25-year-old was credited with 2.03 goals saved above expected against the Rangers. Over his last three outings — all wins — Knight has stopped 92 of 97 shots for a .948 save percentage. While the Rangers outshot and outchanced the Blackhawks by a wide margin, they were credited with only 10 high-danger scoring chances at even strength. Much like Wednesday’s win in Seattle, the Hawks’ defense didn’t allow many threatening looks. The defensemen and forwards also selflessly stepped in the shooting lane, recording 22 blocked shots in Friday’s win. Here are highlights from the Blackhawks 2-1 win over the Rangers, moving their 2026-27 regular-season record to 10-14-2 in 26 games. First Period With Matt Rempe in the penalty box for boarding Kevin Korchinski , the scorching-hot Blackhawks power play hit the ice for the first time and converted. item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 9: Darian DeVries, head coach of the Indiana Hoosiers coaches during the game against the Syracuse Orange at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on November 9, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Indiana men’s basketball dominated Bowling Green tonight, going on a run just over five minutes into the game that effectively put the Falcons to bed. The Hoosiers were shooting well, defending well, and rebounding well in what may have been the most complete performance from this group so far. Though it wasn’t a marquee win like last week’s victories over Arkansas or Kentucky, the margin of victory was one that boosted Indiana’s computer profile. KenPom only favored Indiana by 20 entering the game, so the blowout moved Indiana up five spots in the national ranking. At 8-0, Indiana looks much improved over Darian DeVries’ first season, with KenPom now projecting the Hoosiers to win 23 games and go 12-8 in Big Ten play. Here are 3 Observations from the win: Ball Movement Indiana had a season-high 18 assists tonight against Bowling Green, starting to resemble the fast-paced offense we saw from DeVries’ group last year. While Indiana has more players that are capable of creating unassisted buckets, the ball movement tonight helped the Hoosiers take more quality looks from the perimeter, something that will be important for maintaining a respectable 3-point percentage this season. Bryce Lindsay’s deep shot against Arkansas will go down as a high-point of the season, but over the last couple games Indiana had gotten into the habit of chucking a few too many heat checks from deep or taking transition threes that negate the team’s rebounding advantage. Seeing the way the ball moved tonight was an encouraging step for this group not just cause it made the offense look a little better, but because it reflects well on the team’s chemistry so early in the season. With a team full of transfers, having nine different players record an assist in a game is no small feat. Aiden Sherrell Aiden Sherrell had one of his stronger performances of the season, finishing with 16 points, nine rebounds, two blocks and an assist. He also went 2-6 from 3-point range. Tonight’s performance was a good example of why he’s a potential NBA player. A seven footer who can score from the perimeter, rebound on both ends of the floor, and protect the rim is a valuable piece for any team. After an impressive year last year at Bama, he’s averaging more points and shooting better from deep this year at Indiana. Even though he cooled off by the end of the night, his early threes are exactly what Indiana will need from him going forward. Establishing himself as a threat at the beginning of the game will force defenses to account for him until the final whistle. item.title: Rutgers Women’s Basketball Suffers First Loss of Season, 84-68 to South Dakota State
item.description: Mia Pauldo of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights possesses the ball during an NCAA women's basketball game at Jersey Mike's Arena in Piscataway, United States, on November 16, 2026. (Photo by Dan Squicciarini/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images After starting the season 8-0 and defeating cross-state rival Princeton, Rutgers women’s basketball suffered its first loss of the season, 84-68 to South Dakota State in game one of the Daytona Beach Classic. The Scarlet Knights got off to an ugly start in this game, where they could not dig themselves out of a steep first-quarter hole that saw them down 21 points after just 10 minutes of play. After the game was tied at 5 with just over 8 minutes to play in the first quarter, South Dakota State would go on a 12-0 run to go up 17-5 before the Knights scored again around the four-minute mark in the first quarter. Rutgers would string together four points before the Jackrabbits went on a 13-0 run to close out the quarter up 30-9. The Knights would start to get off the mat over the next two quarters, preventing South Dakota from going on unanswered runs as they did in the first quarter, and eventually closing the gap to single digits as they headed into the fourth quarter down 63-54. However, for every shot the Knights made in the fourth quarter, the Jackrabbits had an answer. A quick three-pointer by South Dakota State’s Hadley Thul at the start of the fourth would put Rutgers in another double-digit hole, one they could not recover from, as the Jackrabbits held on to secure the win. This game highlights some early-season concerns for the Knights, who allowed the Jackrabbits to hit 49.2 percent of their total shots and 52 percent of their shots from three. On top of that, the Jackrabbits forced six more turnovers. recorded 14 more rebounds, had six more points in the paint, and had 15 more assists in their winning effort. Brooklyn Meyer led the Jackrabbits with 20 points, with Katie Vasecka right behind her at 19. Meyer recorded a double-double on the day by scooping up 10 rebounds as well. Emilee Fox and Mali Abdouch recorded double-digit points for South Dakota State as well. Mia Pauldo was once again the star of the show for Rutgers, recording 37 points and hitting half of her shots. In addition to their poor defensive performance, the Knights, outside of Pauldo, failed to drum up any offensive consistency. Outside of Pauldo’s 14 of 28 on all her shots, the rest of the Knights hit just nine of their 38 total shots. While Pauldo is a very effective offensive weapon, scoring has to come from other areas to supplement her efforts. The good news is that the Knights still have time to remedy these issues before Big Ten play starts in full force. The next four games against Georgetown, St. Peter’s, No.19 Ohio State and Seton Hall will provide a glimpse into what the Knights will look like for the rest of the season. item.title: UNC loses ugly, sloppy game to West Virginia
item.description: Nov 27, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; North Carolina Tar Heels head coach Michael Malone pleads his case with the official during the first half against the West Virginia Mountaineers at the Dick Vitale Invitational at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Carolina played the part of a turkey hangover on Friday in an ugly 72-59 loss to West Virginia in the Dick Vitale Invitational. The Tar Heels never led, and even when they tried to mount a comeback in the second half, the Mountaineers promptly stepped on their throats and ended the threat. The tale of the tape really starts and ends with turnovers. Carolina turned the ball over 20 times, directly leading to 28 West Virginia points. Terrence Brown committed eight of those turnovers in a brutal game for a guy the Tar Heels have come to rely on for points. He managed just six on 3-7 shooting. UNC and WVU shot exactly the same percentage from the field at 45%, and Carolina actually made a couple more (11 vs 9) three-pointers. West Virginia had 18 free throw attempts to UNC’s three. The Mountaineers had 14 steals and 11 second chance points. Maximo Adams led the Heels in points 16 points ahead of Jaydon Young with 13 points. Matt Able was scoreless in the first half before hitting a string of three-pointers late to give him 12 points for the game. The highlight of the game for the Tar Heels came when they went on a 12-0 run to cut the deficit to seven points in the second half. West Virginia responded right away with a big run of their own to promptly end any hope that Carolina might steal one they probably had no business stealing. They trailed by as many as 19 halfway through the second half. It has been clear that rebounding is a real issue for this team, and that was on display again tonight. Even though they finished the game only -1 on the boards, there were so many opportunities to keep WVU from getting multiple cracks at a shot or hands that seemed allergic to holding onto a ball. It wasn’t the primary issue in this one (see: turnovers) but it continues to be a real issue. The lack of a real point guard also felt especially prevalent in this mess of a game. Carolina finds itself at the beginning of a considerable stretch of games against Power 4 competition. So far, we’ve seen the games against Georgia and West Virginia end poorly. They’ll face Arkansas in their next game as part of the ACC/SEC challenge. The Razorbacks are coming off a three-point loss to #11 Michigan State.

item.title: Bills Take Down Chiefs Despite Allen’s Struggles on Thanksgiving Day
item.description: The Buffalo Bills are always going to go as far as superstar quarterback Josh Allen takes them, but that doesn’t mean they can’t win big games without a huge performance from him . On Thursday , Buffalo proved that again, defeating Patrick Mahomes and the visiting Kansas City Chiefs to the tune of a 13-10 score at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park. Allen was thankful that his teammates still made things happen that allowed Buffalo to overcome his subpar showing. “I have to better. I need to be better. I will be better,” the former NFL Most Valuable Player Allen said after the game, via John Wawrow of the Associated Press . “Thankful for my team. Thankful for my defense. Thankful for my kicker. Thankful for James Cook and our O-linemen. This took a lot of people,” he added. “I made it a little harder on ourselves. But we found a way to get (win No.) 10.” Bills Take Down Chiefs Despite Allen’s Struggles on Thanksgiving Day Nov 26, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Allen (17) scrambles with the ball against the Chiefs during the third quarter at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Allen only passed for 81 yards with zero touchdowns, while getting picked twice on 10/21 pass completions. But Buffalo’s offense got 117 rushing yards and a touchdown from James Cook III on 32 carries, while the defense held Mahomes to just 174 passing yards on 16/29 completions with zero scores. Allen isn’t always going to be at the top of his game, so it was great for Buffalo to see the other units and players stepping up and delivering the goods when the team’s most important player is struggling. It emanated from the upper reaches of the building and cascaded to the ice during the Blue Jackets' 2-0 loss to the Detroit Red Wings . More: Devils drop Blue Jackets in shootout: Where's the fight? item.title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. Signs One-Year Deal With Blue Jays
item.description: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Jazz Chisholm Jr. has left the New York Yankees to join their AL East rival, the Toronto Blue Jays. ESPN reported on Friday afternoon that the two-time All-Star signed a one-year contract worth $20 million. A $16 million player option for the 2028 season and a $6 million signing bonus are part of the deal. This move keeps Chisholm in the division while shifting him to a team that finished last in the East last year. The contract structure offers a unique twist for the 28-year-old infielder. Should Chisholm decline his $16 million player option next year, Toronto’s deal becomes a $40 million team option. This clause gives the player leverage while providing the Blue Jays with a safety net if they wish to retain him long-term. The signing comes as the Yankees face uncertainty in their own lineup construction for the upcoming season. Chisholm’s Recent Performance and Value Chisholm brings a mix of power and speed to Toronto , though his 2026 numbers were modest. He hit 19 home runs and drove in 55 runs while stealing 41 bases for the Yankees last season. His batting line ended at .231/.312/.399, which resulted in 1.7 wins above replacement. These figures show a player who still generates runs but struggled to find consistent contact in the previous year. The year before, in 2025, Chisholm posted much stronger results, earning him a Silver Slugger Award. He recorded 31 home runs, 80 RBIs, and 31 stolen bases with a .481 slugging percentage. That performance proved he could be a top-tier contributor when healthy and in rhythm. The Blue Jays hope he can return to that form after moving to a new ballpark and lineup. Chisholm has played multiple positions throughout his career, adding flexibility to his contract value. He started with the Miami Marlins as a shortstop and center fielder before the trade to New York. During his time in the Bronx, he played third base and second base. This versatility allows Toronto to plug him into various spots in their infield mix alongside Ernie Clement and Andrés Giménez. General Manager Brian Cashman has been open about the lack of guarantees for the upcoming roster. BC came in 7-0, a day removed from a last-second win over UCF, and as a 9.5-point underdog. The Bearcats handed BC its first loss of the season, 70-59, pulling away in the second half. The start was promising. Tyler Tejada hit two early threes to put Cincinnati up 6-1, but BC turned five Bearcat turnovers into a 13-0 run and led 14-6 after a Money Williams layup at the 12:14 mark. Williams scored 10 points during that stretch. Then the offense dried up. Former BC forward Jayden Hastings started a Cincinnati run with two free throws, and the Bearcats took a 20-19 lead on an Elijah Perryman layup with just over five minutes left in the half. The teams traded baskets until two Armoni Zeigler free throws gave BC a 28-27 halftime lead. Cincinnati committed 10 turnovers in the first half, and BC held an 11-3 edge in points off turnovers at the break. That’s the primary reason BC was ahead. Cincinnati cleaned that up after halftime. A Colby Duggan three put BC up 31-29, but the Bearcats scored the next six to lead 35-31. Williams tied it at 36 with a second-chance three at 15:18. Cincinnati then went on a 12-2 run, capped by a Tylen Riley steal and breakaway dunk, to lead 48-38 with 10:54 left. BC never got even again. To BC’s credit, it didn’t go away. item.description: Adrian Morejon Yankees Getty According to an MLB insider, the New York Yankees are getting “ultra aggressive” in their pursuit of top free-agent reliever Adrian Morejon. The Yankees have already brought back their own free agents, David Bednar and Tim Hill, plus they inked Brent Suter and Jonathan Loaisiga. But New York isn’t stopping there, as they want the biggest fish in the free-agent reliever pond this winter: Morejon. Yankees Badly Want Adrian Morejon Per MLB insider Bob Nightengale, the Yankees are doing everything that they can to sign Morejon, who has pitched the past eight seasons for the San Diego Padres. “The New York Yankees, who have already spent $48.4 million on free agent relievers this winter, have made free-agent lefty Adrian Morejon their No. 1 priority and have become ultra-aggressive in their active pursuit to sign him before the lockout, persons involved with negotiations say,” Nightengale wrote on X . The New York Yankees, who have already spent $48.4 million on free agent relievers this winter, have made free-agent lefty Adrian Morejon their No. 1 priority and have become ultra-aggressive in their active pursuit to sign him before the lockout, persons involved with… — Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) November 27, 2026 Adrian Morejon Will Get a Huge Contract Based on the going rate for free-agent pitching that we’ve seen so far this offseason, it seems clear that Morejon is going to get a huge contract in free agency. At a minimum, it feels like Morejon is going to get a five-year, $100 million deal, but he may get even more. It’s a lot of money to pay for a relief pitcher, but Morejon is about as elite as it gets from the left side. With so many teams trying to sign him, including the rival Toronto Blue Jays, Yankees GM Brian Cashman clearly feels like this is the guy that he needs to get to transform his bullpen into one of the very best in the entire league. If the Yankees do sign Morejon , he will be leaving the National League for the first time in his MLB career to pitch for an American League team, and he’ll be heading to the pressure cooker that is the AL East, to boot. But Morejon’s stuff is about as elite as it gets in the league from the left-hand side, and if the Yankees sign the fireballer, it makes their bullpen that much more dangerous heading into next season.
